neighbours.label: interrogative or exclamative ' what' opening a question or outcry, often in quoted speech (what shall I do?, what big eyes)
fire: The old woman wrung her hands and cried, "Oh dear, what shall become of us now?"
He stared at the broken window and asked his brother, "What happened here last night?"
"My goodness," said the girl, "what a strange little house this is!"
She turned to the stranger and whispered, "What do you want from me?"
The knight fell to his knees: "Alas, what have I done to deserve this?"
When the letter arrived, my mother gasped, "What on earth is this?"
The child looked up at the wolf and said, "Grandmother, what sharp teeth you have!"
In the silence the sailor muttered, "What is that light out on the water?"
quiet: The old woman wrung her hands, saying she would give them what they needed.
He stared at the broken window and finally understood what happened there last night.
The girl said the little house had what every family wants: a warm fire.
She turned to the stranger and offered him what remained of the bread.
The knight fell to his knees and accepted what the king had decided.
When the letter arrived, my mother read what my father had written.
The child looked up at the wolf and did what her grandmother had taught her.
In the silence the sailor wrote down what he had seen on the water.

notes: card: top examples are ' what' in lamenting questions; + pole is free-relative ' what' (has what we need). Near misses use free-relative what.
